notes: The KTDB (Korea Transport Database) national passenger O/D update rebuilds the base-year (2023) trip matrix and forecasts demand to 2050. Two zone systems are reconciled: 250 si-gun-gu zones nationwide, and finer eup-myeon-dong zones inside six metro areas (Seoul Capital Area, Busan-Ulsan, Daegu, Gwangju, Daejeon-Sejong-Chungcheong, Jeju). Base-year O/D is built mode by mode: bus/rail use actual ridership statistics; private-car and other personal modes go through a five-step expansion combining travel-survey samples, telecom big data, and card/TCS data, with bidirectional and zero-cell corrections. The draft O/D is validated against observed traffic counts via cordon-line/screenline %ERROR checks and FHWA-style assignment validation, iterating until errors meet tolerance. Socioeconomic indicators (population, employment, enrollment, land-use plans) are projected per target year, then a standard four-step model (generation/attraction, distribution, mode split, assignment) is applied consistently across national and regional models to produce future O/D matrices.
